description: A six-circuit 30-amp manual transfer switch kit with the PB30 inlet box and cord included, the default safe hookup for a 5,000 to 7,500 watt portable with an L14-30 outlet.

verdict: The 31406CRK is the transfer switch most electricians reach for when a homeowner arrives with a portable generator. It is our top pick because it bundles everything a 30-amp portable hookup needs.

**How it works.** It is a small prewired panel that mounts beside your main breaker panel, with a flexible conduit whip that enters the panel through a knockout. Six chosen circuits move onto it, and each gets a Line/Off/Gen switch. Because every circuit is switched individually, generator power can only reach those circuits and never back-feed the utility lines.

**Six circuits, budgeted.** A 240V load such as a well pump takes two positions. A typical list: well pump (two), furnace, fridge, freezer and one lighting circuit. If you need more, the [31410CRK](/gear/reliance-31410crk/) gives you ten.

**The kit part matters.** CRK means it includes the [PB30 power inlet box](/gear/reliance-pb30/) and a 10-foot 30-amp cord, so the generator plugs into an outside wall instead of a cord through a window. It is rated for 30-amp, 125/250V generators with an [L14-30](/glossary/l14-30/) outlet, up to 7,500 running watts. At 240 volts, 30 amps is 7,200 watts, which is the real ceiling.

Owners and electricians report a fast, tidy install; the common complaint is that six circuits fill up quickly. It still needs a licensed electrician and usually a permit. It leads our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide; see also our [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/) explainer.

faqs.q: What size generator works with the Reliance 31406CRK?
faqs.a: Portables with a 120/240V, 30-amp L14-30 outlet, typically 5,000 to 7,500 running watts. Reliance rates it for generators up to 7,500 running watts, and a 30-amp, 240V circuit carries at most 7,200 watts. Larger generators work but cannot deliver more than the switch allows; for 50-amp outlets, use a 50-amp inlet with an interlock or a 50-amp switch.

Count your circuits. The 31406CRK has six positions; the [31410CRK](/gear/reliance-31410crk/) has ten. Both are 30-amp kits with the PB30 inlet and a cord. A well pump takes two positions, so if your list includes a 240V pump plus a furnace, fridge, freezer, sump pump and two lighting circuits, you need the ten-circuit model.

verdict: The 31410CRK is the same proven design as the [31406CRK](/gear/reliance-31406crk/), with four more circuits. Choose it when six positions will not cover your list.

**Why ten helps.** Every 240V load takes two positions. A well pump (two), a furnace, a fridge, a freezer, a sump pump, a garage door circuit and three lighting or outlet circuits fill all ten. With six positions you would have to drop half of that.

**Same 30-amp ceiling.** More circuits do not mean more power. It is still a 30-amp, 125/250V switch rated for generators up to 7,500 running watts, and 30 amps at 240 volts is 7,200 watts. Use the [wattage calculator](/tools/generator-wattage-calculator/) to make sure the loads on those ten circuits fit what your generator makes, and use the Line/Off/Gen switches to shed loads as needed.

**What is in the kit.** The CRK kit adds the [PB30](/gear/reliance-pb30/) outdoor inlet box and a 10-foot 30-amp cord, so the generator connects at an outside wall through an [L14-30](/glossary/l14-30/) plug. The switch mounts beside the main panel and connects through a prewired whip.

Owners and electricians report a tidy install; the common complaint is that the wider cabinet needs more wall space beside the panel. It needs a licensed electrician and usually a permit. It ranks in our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide.

faqs.q: Does the Reliance 31410CRK let you use a bigger generator?
faqs.a: No. Ten circuits give you more choice of what to power, not more power. It is a 30-amp, 125/250V switch rated for up to 7,500 running watts, and 30 amps at 240 volts is 7,200 watts. For a generator with a 50-amp outlet, a 50-amp inlet such as the PBN50 with a panel interlock lets you use more of its output.

faqs.q: How many circuits do you need in a generator transfer switch?
faqs.a: List your must-run loads and count 240V loads twice. A common list is a well pump (two), furnace, fridge, freezer, sump pump and a couple of lighting circuits, which is eight positions. That points to a ten-circuit switch like the 31410CRK. A home on city water with gas heat often fits in six.

name: Reliance Controls TF151W
amazon: Reliance Controls TF151W furnace transfer switch
description: A single-circuit 15-amp, 120-volt transfer switch that mounts at the furnace, so a small generator can run a gas or oil furnace safely without moving circuits at the panel.
quick: 15A, single circuit, 120V, mounts at the furnace. A single-circuit 15-amp, 120-volt transfer switch that mounts at the furnace, so a small generator can run a gas or oil furnace safely without moving circuits at the panel.
bestFor: Running a gas or oil furnace from a small generator
skipIf: You want to power more than the furnace
specs: 15A, single circuit, 120V, mounts at the furnace
verdict: The TF151W solves one problem well: keeping a gas or oil furnace running from a small generator. In cold climates, that is often the most important load in an outage.

**Why a furnace needs it.** A furnace's blower, inducer and controls draw only a few hundred watts, but they are hardwired, so you cannot plug them into a cord. The TF151W replaces or sits beside the furnace's service switch and lets the furnace run from either its normal circuit or a generator, with no back-feed path to the grid.

**Small generator friendly.** It is a 15-amp, 120-volt, single-circuit switch. At 120 volts, 15 amps is 1,800 watts, far more than a furnace needs, so a small [inverter generator](/glossary/inverter-generator/) like the [Honda EU2200i](/gear/honda-eu2200i/) can carry it. No 240-volt generator and no work at the main panel are required. Furnace control boards can be sensitive, so a generator with low [THD](/glossary/thd/) is the safer match.

**Its limit.** It powers the furnace and nothing else. If you also want the fridge, freezer and sump pump, a six-circuit switch like the [31406CRK](/gear/reliance-31406crk/) covers the furnace and those loads together.

Owners report a quick install and peace of mind in winter; the main complaint is the single-circuit limit. Have an electrician confirm it suits your furnace and local code. It appears in our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide.

faqs.q: What size generator do you need for the Reliance TF151W?
faqs.a: A small one. Most gas furnace blowers, inducers and controls draw a few hundred watts, and the switch is rated for 15 amps at 120 volts, or 1,800 watts. A 2,000- to 3,000-watt inverter generator is plenty and protects the furnace control board with clean power. Check the furnace nameplate amps to be sure.

faqs.q: Can the TF151W power anything besides the furnace?
faqs.a: No. It is a single-circuit switch that carries only the furnace circuit it is wired into. To back up the fridge, freezer, sump pump and lights as well, use a multi-circuit switch such as the six-circuit Reliance 31406CRK, which can include the furnace as one of its circuits and costs less than several single-circuit switches.

name: Reliance Controls PB30
amazon: Reliance Controls PB30 power inlet box
description: Reliance's 30-amp outdoor power inlet box with an L14-30 inlet, the outside half of most portable generator hookups, sold alone or inside the CRK switch kits.
quick: 30A, L14-30 inlet, outdoor enclosure. Reliance's 30-amp outdoor power inlet box with an L14-30 inlet, the outside half of most portable generator hookups, sold alone or inside the CRK switch kits.
bestFor: Connecting a 30-amp portable at an outside wall
skipIf: Your generator has only a 50-amp outlet
specs: Up to about 7,500 running watts (7,200 W at 30A × 240V)
verdict: The PB30 is the outside half of a safe generator hookup. It lets you plug the generator into the wall of the house instead of running cords through a window.

**What it does.** It is a weatherproof NEMA 3R box with a 30-amp, 125/250V [L14-30](/glossary/l14-30/) male inlet. An electrician mounts it on an exterior wall and wires it to a [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/) or a breaker held by an [interlock kit](/glossary/interlock-kit/). In an outage you run a 30-amp cord like the [PC3020](/gear/reliance-pc3020/) from the generator's L14-30R outlet to the box.

**Sizing.** A 30-amp, 240-volt connection carries at most 7,200 watts, which suits portables up to about 7,500 running watts. Bigger generators with a 50-amp outlet need the [PBN50](/gear/reliance-pbn50/) instead, plus a 50-amp switch or interlock breaker.

**Buy it alone or in a kit.** The PB30 already comes inside the 31406CRK and 31410CRK kits. Buy it on its own when you use an interlock kit, or when your switch did not include an inlet. Placement matters: put it where the generator can sit at least 20 feet from doors and windows without a long cord run.

Owners and electricians report it is sturdy and simple; the most common mistake is mounting it where the generator ends up beside a window. It appears in our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide.

Matches the most common portable outlet

Budget tier
cons: Already included in CRK kits, so check before buying

faqs.q: Do you need a PB30 if you have an interlock kit?
faqs.a: Yes, or another 30-amp inlet. An interlock kit only prevents the main breaker and generator breaker from being on together; it does not give you a place to plug in. The PB30 provides the outdoor L14-30 inlet, wired to the interlocked breaker in your panel, so the generator connects safely from outside.

faqs.q: PB30 vs PBN50: which inlet box do you need?
faqs.a: Match your generator's outlet. The PB30 has a 30-amp L14-30 inlet for generators up to about 7,500 running watts. The [PBN50](/gear/reliance-pbn50/) has a 50-amp, 125/250V California-style inlet for larger generators. A 50-amp inlet only helps if the switch or interlock breaker and the wiring are also rated for 50 amps.

name: Reliance Controls PBN50
amazon: Reliance Controls PBN50 power inlet box
description: Reliance's 50-amp outdoor inlet box with a California-style twist-lock inlet, for large portables when the switch or interlock breaker and wiring are all rated for 50 amps.
quick: 50A, 125/250V California-style inlet, outdoor enclosure. Reliance's 50-amp outdoor inlet box with a California-style twist-lock inlet, for large portables when the switch or interlock breaker and wiring are all rated for 50 amps.
bestFor: Large portables with a 50-amp outlet and a 50-amp interlock
skipIf: Your switch or breaker is only 30 amps
verdict: The PBN50 is the inlet box for big portables. Buy it only when the whole path, from generator to panel, is rated for 50 amps.

**What it does.** It is a NEMA 3R outdoor box with a 50-amp, 125/250V California-style twist-lock inlet. Larger portables, usually 9,000 running watts and up, often have this outlet alongside or instead of the L14-30. At 240 volts, 50 amps is 12,000 watts, enough to run central air on a large portable plus essentials.

**The whole path has to match.** Generator outlet, cord, inlet, wiring and the switch or breaker must all be rated for 50 amps. A 50-amp inlet feeding a 30-amp switch gains you nothing. That makes the PBN50 most useful with a panel [interlock kit](/glossary/interlock-kit/), where the generator breaker can be sized to the generator, or with a 50-amp [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/).

**Check your plug.** Many generators, like the [Westinghouse WGen9500DF](/gear/westinghouse-wgen9500df/), have a 14-50R outlet rather than a California-style twist-lock, so you need a cord made for that pairing. Adapters that change amperage are a bad idea on a circuit like this. For 30-amp generators, the [PB30](/gear/reliance-pb30/) is the right box.
Owners and electricians report solid construction; the common complaint is the cost of a matching 50-amp cord. It appears in our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide.

faqs.q: What generators work with the Reliance PBN50?
faqs.a: Generators with a 120/240V, 50-amp outlet, typically 9,000 running watts and up. Many have a California-style twist-lock outlet, which matches with a standard cord; others have a 14-50R, which needs a cord made for that pairing. The switch or interlock breaker and the wiring must also be rated for 50 amps to use more than 30.

faqs.q: Is a 50-amp inlet worth it over 30 amps?
faqs.a: Only if your generator makes more than about 7,200 running watts. A 30-amp, 240V connection tops out at 7,200 watts; 50 amps allows up to 12,000. For a 9,500-watt generator, that is the difference between using about three-quarters of its output and all of it, provided the switch or interlock breaker is also 50 amps.

name: Reliance Controls PC3020
amazon: Reliance Controls PC3020 30 amp generator cord
description: Reliance's 20-foot, 30-amp generator cord with L14-30 ends, the link between a portable's twist-lock outlet and a PB30 inlet box when 10 feet is not enough.
quick: 30A, L14-30 plug to L14-30 connector, 20 ft. Reliance's 20-foot, 30-amp generator cord with L14-30 ends, the link between a portable's twist-lock outlet and a PB30 inlet box when 10 feet is not enough.

specs: 30A, L14-30 plug to L14-30 connector, 20 ft
verdict: The PC3020 is the cord that connects a portable generator to an inlet box. Buy it when you need more distance than the 10-foot cord in Reliance's kits.

**Why length matters.** Generators should sit at least 20 feet from doors, windows and vents. If your inlet box is near a door, a 10-foot cord forces the generator too close. The 20-foot PC3020 gives you room to park it safely and point the exhaust away from the house.

**Match the plugs.** It has a 30-amp, 125/250V [L14-30](/glossary/l14-30/) plug on one end and an L14-30 connector on the other, so it fits a generator's L14-30R outlet and a [PB30](/gear/reliance-pb30/) inlet. It is four-conductor, carrying both hots, neutral and ground for 120/240V. At 240 volts, 30 amps is 7,200 watts, so it suits portables up to about 7,500 running watts.

**Do not cheap out here.** A cord this long carrying near-full load needs heavy conductors to limit voltage drop, which matters for motor loads like well pumps. A properly rated name-brand cord is worth it over a thin generic one.

Owners report solid build and secure twist-lock ends; the common complaint is that it is stiff to coil in cold weather. It belongs with a [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/) kit like the [31406CRK](/gear/reliance-31406crk/), and it appears in our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide.

faqs.q: Is a 20-foot generator cord long enough?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Safety guidance calls for at least 20 feet between the generator and doors, windows and vents, so a 20-foot cord works if the inlet box is away from openings. If the inlet sits beside a door, you may need a longer cord or a better inlet location. Avoid chaining cords together.

faqs.q: Can the PC3020 plug into a regular household outlet?
faqs.a: No. It has 30-amp L14-30 twist-lock ends, which fit only an L14-30R outlet on the generator and an L14-30 inlet box such as the PB30. That is by design: back-feeding a house through a regular outlet with a double-male cord is dangerous and illegal. Use an inlet box with a transfer switch or interlock.

verdict: The HomeLink 6853 is the strongest rival to the Reliance kits, and the better pick if you want breaker-style circuits with room to grow. It comes with everything a 30-amp portable hookup needs.

**Breakers, not toggles.** Instead of individual Line/Off/Gen toggles, it is a small subpanel with its own breakers: one 30-amp 2-pole, one 20-amp and five 15-amp single-pole breakers, for eight circuits in ten spaces. The 2-pole 30-amp suits a 240V well pump. Generac notes it accepts arc-fault and GFCI breakers, which some local codes require when circuits move.

**30-amp ceiling.** It is a 30-amp, 125/250V switch, so 7,200 watts at 240 volts is the limit, which fits most 6,500- to 8,000-watt portables like the [Generac GP8000E](/gear/generac-gp8000e/). Size your circuits with the [wattage calculator](/tools/generator-wattage-calculator/).

Owners and electricians report a clean install and like the expansion room; the common complaint is that the 10-foot cord is short for safe generator placement. Compare it with the six-circuit [Reliance 31406CRK](/gear/reliance-31406crk/) in our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide.

faqs.q: Can the Generac 6853 run a well pump?
faqs.a: Yes. It includes a 2-pole 30-amp breaker, the type a 240V well pump circuit uses, and the switch is rated 30 amps at 125/250V. The pump still needs a generator large enough to start it; a 6,500- to 8,000-watt portable covers a typical 1 HP pump plus essentials, connected through the included inlet box and cord.

name: GenerLink MA23-S
amazon: GenerLink MA23-S meter collar transfer switch
description: A 30-amp meter collar transfer switch that installs between the electric meter and its socket, letting a 240V portable under 8,500 running watts feed the house with no panel rewiring.
quick: 30A meter collar, under 8,500W generators, surge protection. A 30-amp meter collar transfer switch that installs between the electric meter and its socket, letting a 240V portable under 8,500 running watts feed the house with no panel rewiring.
bestFor: Panel-free hookup where your utility allows meter collars
skipIf: Your utility does not permit customer meter collars
specs: Generator inlet on the collar; generator needs a 240V four-prong outlet
verdict: GenerLink is the transfer switch with no work inside your panel. It installs behind your electric meter, but only where your utility allows it, so check that before anything else.

**How it works.** The MA23-S is a collar that fits between the meter and the meter socket. You plug a 240V portable into its inlet, and when it senses generator power with the grid down, it disconnects the utility and feeds the house through the meter socket. It is listed to UL 1008M, the standard for meter-socket transfer switches. See [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/) for how isolation prevents back-feed.

**Sizing.** The MA23 is the 30-amp model, for portables with running watts under 8,500, and the generator needs a 240V four-prong outlet such as an [L14-30R](/glossary/l14-30/). Because the whole panel is live, you manage loads by switching breakers off; use the [wattage calculator](/tools/generator-wattage-calculator/) to stay under your generator's rating. The S suffix adds 75kA-per-phase surge protection. The 40-amp MA24 suits generators under 10,000 running watts.

**The catch is the utility.** Acceptance varies. Some utilities, such as AEP Texas, have accepted GenerLink models, while others, such as PPL Electric, do not allow customer-owned meter collars at all. Where allowed, installation is usually done by the utility or an approved installer.

Owners report fast installs with no panel work; the common complaints are utility restrictions and managing loads by breaker. Compare panel-side options in our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide.

faqs.q: Is GenerLink allowed by my utility?
faqs.a: It depends on the utility. Some, such as AEP Texas, have accepted the MA23 and MA24 models as meter collar devices; others, such as PPL Electric, do not permit customer-owned devices between the meter and meter base. Call your utility first. Where it is allowed, the utility or an approved installer usually does the install.

faqs.q: GenerLink MA23-S vs MA24-S: what is the difference?
faqs.a: Amperage. The MA23-S is the 30-amp model, for portables under 8,500 running watts. The MA24-S is the 40-amp model, for portables under 10,000 running watts. Both include 75kA-per-phase surge protection, shown by the S suffix, and both need a generator with a 240V four-prong outlet. Match the model to your generator.

name: Generac RXSW200A3
amazon: Generac RXSW200A3 200 amp automatic transfer switch
description: Generac's 200-amp service-rated automatic transfer switch, the whole-house switch for Guardian standby generators, in an outdoor aluminum NEMA 3R enclosure.
quick: 200A service-rated ATS, NEMA 3R, Generac generators only. Generac's 200-amp service-rated automatic transfer switch, the whole-house switch for Guardian standby generators, in an outdoor aluminum NEMA 3R enclosure.
bestFor: Whole-house Guardian installs on a 200-amp service
skipIf: You are connecting a portable generator
specs: Automatic transfer switch, service entrance rated
Generac single-phase standby with Evolution or Nexus controller
verdict: The RXSW200A3 is the whole-house automatic switch that pairs with Generac's Guardian standby generators. If you are installing a Guardian on a 200-amp service, this is the switch your installer is likely to quote.

**Service rated is the point.** It is a 200-amp, 120/240V single-phase switch rated for service entrance use, so it can serve as the main disconnect between the meter and the house. That lets the installer put it outside between the meter and the main panel rather than adding a subpanel inside, which often simplifies a whole-house install.

**Automatic, not manual.** When the grid drops, the generator's controller senses it, starts the engine and the switch moves the whole house to generator power; when the grid returns, it switches back and the generator cools down and stops. Unlike a manual [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/) for a portable, nobody has to be home.

**Match the generator.** Generac lists it for Generac single-phase generators with Evolution or Nexus controllers only, such as the [Guardian 22kW](/gear/generac-guardian-22kw/) or [26kW](/gear/generac-guardian-26kw/). With a 200-amp switch on a 22kW generator, large loads like a second AC may need load management so the generator is not overloaded. It is housed in an aluminum NEMA 3R enclosure.

Owners and installers report a clean, reliable switchover; the main complaint is that it ties you to Generac generators. For portable hookups, see our [generator transfer switch](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) guide, and read up on [standby generator](/glossary/standby-generator/) basics.
pros: 200A, service entrance rated
Fully automatic switchover and return

cons: Needs load management when the generator is smaller than peak demand

faqs.q: Does the Generac RXSW200A3 work with other generator brands?
faqs.a: No. Generac lists it for use with Generac single-phase generators that use an Evolution or Nexus controller, such as current Guardian air-cooled models. The controller and switch work as a system. Kohler and Champion standby generators use their own automatic transfer switches, such as the aXis switches Champion bundles with its 14kW unit.

faqs.q: What does service rated mean on a transfer switch?
faqs.a: A service-rated switch, like the RXSW200A3, includes a breaker that can act as the main service disconnect, so it can be installed between the utility meter and the main panel. A non-service-rated switch goes after an existing main breaker. Service-rated switches often simplify whole-house installs on a 200-amp service, but local code decides which you need.
